SPECTRA_EXTRACTION.md.text:
# Fig 5A / 5B / 5C and Fig S14: full-resolution extraction (SPECTRA_EXTRACTION)

Built 2026-10-06 on branch `spectra`. Scripts: `_extraction_scripts/fig5lib.py`, `fig5_spectra.py`, `fig5_v2_crosscheck.py`, `s14lib.py`, `s14_spectra.py` (re-runnable; they call `pdfimages`).
Crops used: `../deep/crops/fig5*`, `../deep/crops/figS14_*`.

## 1. Sources and method (vector vs bitmap)

| Figure | Best source | Native pixels | Vector? | Method |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Fig 5 A/B/C | bioRxiv v3 PDF p.9 (`pdfimages -list`: image 1951x1098, 300 ppi, RGB + soft mask) = same design as the published JPG (787x445, lower res) | 1951x1098 | **No.** `pdftocairo -svg` page 9 has 2 `<image>` elements; no polyline longer than a tick. The older 600-dpi "render" used earlier was an upsample of this 300-ppi raster. | BITMAP: per-pixel-column height, sub-pixel top edge, x calibration below |
| Fig 5 (older rendering) | v2 p.9 (1985x1138 indexed, 306 ppi); v1/v4 p.9 (1296x743) | | No | used only as a cross-check (section 3) |
| Fig S14 Part I / II (spectrum + TIC, 4 panels) | SM PDF p.21 (1396x1074) / p.22 (1422x1038), `sciadv.aec7048_sm.pdf` (v3 PDF has the same rasters) | native | **No** (Xcalibur screenshots) | BITMAP |

Resolution limits that matter: a 5A pixel is **3.07 m/z** wide and **0.74 % (A) / 0.26 % (B,C)** tall; an S14 pixel is 1.39 m/z and 0.27 % tall. Each isotope line of a Q-Exactive profile is far sub-pixel, so all heights are the apex of the drawn envelope; **areas are not usable** (a pixel sum measures the line rendering).

### x calibration of Fig 5 (fixed)
* Slope: 93 x-axis tick marks per panel (20 m/z minor, 100 m/z major; major #1 = 200, #19 = 2000). Slope 0.32570 px per m/z in A1-A4 (0.3257 +- 0.0001), 0.3553 (B), 0.3562 (C); tick rms residual 0.3 px.
* **The tick axis is not registered to the data.** Offsets between the tick axis and the printed peak labels: B +10.3 m/z, C +3.4 m/z, A1 -4.2, A2 -3.0, A3 -3.4, A4 -0.7. This is why the old `fig5A_channel_peaks.csv` was "ambiguous by +-5": it used the ticks. The old `fig5_BC_profiles.csv` has its peaks +9..+11 m/z (B) and +1..+7 m/z (C) away from the printed labels for the same reason (heights in it are fine).
* Offset: fitted to the printed peak labels (B: 4 peaks, residuals -0.21/-0.10/+0.22/+0.09 m/z; C: 5 peaks, residuals -0.13/-0.18/-0.07/+0.04/+0.34 m/z; each A panel: its one main peak, which fixes the offset only to 0.3 px = 1 m/z). The B/C fits also confirm the tick slope to <0.15 % over 570 m/z.
* Independent check inside A: A1's z=10 blip lands at 857.5 (theory 857.49); the 403 and 171 chemical peaks of A4 land 0.9 m/z above the B/C values of the same peaks (402.5, 170.1), A3's land 1.8 m/z below. A-panel m/z uncertainty (1 sigma) is therefore **~1 m/z (A1, A2, A4), ~2 m/z (A3)**; `mz_best_estimate` below removes the offset against 5C.
* y: 0 = centre of the x-axis spine, 100 = y-axis tick; heights are 100.7-101.3 for the main peaks (the line cap extends ~1 px above the 100 tick), so all ratios use the measured main-peak height.

## 2. Noise floors and display limits (the honest floor)

`fig5A_noise_windows.csv` has, per panel and per z=5..11 window (centre +- (3 sigma isotope envelope /z + 2.0 m/z); sigma(C378H629N105O118S) = 1.279 Da, so the envelope half-width alone is 0.77 (z=5) .. 0.35 (z=11) m/z), the in-window and local (+-100 m/z) height statistics.

* **In all four v3/published A panels the baseline is exactly flat: median = p95 = 0 % everywhere outside peaks.** There is no measurable noise floor in the figure. What limits detection is the *display*: the x-axis spine is 2.2-3.0 px thick and hides everything below its half-thickness. Certain-detection limit (spine half-thickness + 0.5 px): **A1 1.27 %, A2 1.21 %, A3 1.48 %, A4 1.18 %, B 0.52 %, C 0.62 %** of the panel's base peak. One pixel = 0.74 % (A).
* The smallest visible 5A features are 1-px bumps of 1.5 % (A2, 3 of them) to 3 % (A4); the three nearest-to-limit bumps in A2 are exactly 1.54 %.
* **The plotting is suppressing low content.** The same A panels in bioRxiv v1/v2 (older plot style) show a real baseline: 28-67 % of baseline columns carry 1-px blips (0.7-1.1 %), p95 of the blank baseline = 0.9-1.1 %, none above 2 % outside catalogued peaks (`fig5A_crosstalk_v2_crosscheck.csv` header). The v3/published redraw shows none of them, i.e. it either thresholds at ~1.2 % or draws with a heavier spine. So the true raw-data noise is ~1 % of base peak (comparable with a 1-px blip), and **no 5A panel can say anything below ~1.2-1.5 %**. Orbitrap (Q Exactive) profile data also have no hard intensity floor; I could not determine any acquisition threshold from the figure.
* Windows contain 1-3 columns only (3 m/z/px), so "median/p95 in the window" is degenerate (0); the local +-100 m/z columns (n = 35-67 per window) are 0 / 0 except where the window sits on the sideband of an adduct peak.
* **Overlaps.** No window of z=5..11 coincides with the low-mass chemical peaks (<=575 m/z). The only other non-zero structure near a neighbour window is the +269/+457 Da adduct sideband pair of 9+ (982.5, 1003.5 m/z), which is 68-89 m/z below the z=8 window of the 9+ panel and not part of it. The 6+ panel's 1412.8 shoulder is 15.7 m/z from its main peak and does not touch the z=7 window.
* Chance coincidence (`p_chance`, random blip at the panel's blip density): 0.7-2.5 % per window; for the two simultaneous bumps in A2 (9+ and 7+) about 1e-4.

## 3. New cross-talk targets (Fig 5A / 5C)

T(z_n)/T(z_ch) = (panel height ratio) / (5C height ratio), `fig5A_crosstalk_matrix.csv` (value, lower, upper = all heights +-1 px, kind). "upper-limit" uses the display limit above (a peak that tall would be seen) and the source minus 1 px.

| Quantity | Old target | New (v3 / published) | New, bioRxiv v2 rendering |
|---|---|---|---|
| 9+ channel, T(10+)/T(9+) | 0.27 | **0.272** (0.229-0.321), measured, panel 8.55 % at 857.5 m/z | **< 0.040** (no peak above 1.1 %) |
| 9+ channel, T(8+)/T(9+) | < 0.002 | **0.0030** (0.0018-0.0042), 1-px bump (2.0 %), marginal; **not** < 0.002 | **0.0130**, a real 8.8 % peak at 1069-1072 |
| 9+ channel, T(7+)/T(9+) | - | < 0.0032 | < 0.0031 |
| 6+ channel, T(7+)/T(6+) | < 0.013 | **< 0.0031** (4x tighter) | < 0.0032 |
| 6+ channel, T(8+)/T(6+) | - | < 0.0019 | < 0.0019 |

Our model values (0.016 for 10+/9+, 0.44 for 7+/6+) are therefore off by x17 (low) and x140 (high, vs the limit) with the published figure.

Other reading of the matrix: the 8+ channel shows 9+ (T ~ 0.10, 0.05-0.15) and 7+ (T ~ 0.025, 0.013-0.038) as 1-px bumps (marginal; the coincidence with the expected m/z of both neighbours at the panel's blip density has p ~ 1e-4, so they are probably real but their size is only good to a factor 2). The 7+ channel shows nothing: T(8+)/T(7+) < 0.0089, T(6+) < 0.057. **The only clear cross-talk in the published figure is 10+ in the 9+ channel (T = 0.27). Every other neighbour is either a limit (< 0.0019 .. < 0.28; the loosest are the z=10 limits in the 7+/8+ channels, 0.20 and 0.27) or a marginal 1-px bump (A1: 8+ 0.003; A2: 9+ 0.10, 7+ 0.025).**

## 4. Differences between figure versions (surprising)

* **Panel A1 changed between v2 and v3/published.** v1/v2: 9+ channel shows an 8.8 % peak at ~+117 m/z (the 8+ ion) and no 10+ (<=1.1 %). v3/published: 10+ at 8.55 % (m/z 857.5, exactly the 10+ value) and a 2 % bump at 8+. A2-A4 and the control are unchanged within pixel noise (A4's 330/403/505/575 peaks are 10.4/24.8/2.2/2.9 % in v2 vs 10.9/25.5/2.9/3.8 % in v3). So A1 was re-plotted/re-acquired (and 5C's 6+ label changed 1428.458 -> 1428.258). The quoted old target 0.27 comes from the final version; the earlier version gave T(8+)/T(9+) = 0.013 and no 10+ leak. Ask the authors which A1 is the real one.
* In the final A1 the cross-talk is on the LOW-m/z side (10+ is 95 m/z below 9+); the 8+ side is down at T ~ 0.003.

## 5. Transfer function (`fig5_transfer_function.csv`)

T_k(species)/T_k(main) = (panel_k/panel_k(main)) / (5C/5C(main)) for every 5C peak >= its display limit (0.62 %) and every peak that appears in a 5A panel but not in 5C. Each panel is normalised to its own base peak, so only within-panel ratios exist; absolute T and T between channels cannot be recovered. Control must be >= 3x its limit (1.87 %) for a two-sided T; otherwise kind = lower-limit (panel peak with control below that) or control_below_3x_floor (no information). Highlights:

* Same-charge adduct series (sidebands of +258..+269 Da on 8+, 9+, 7+, i.e. 1103.9 / 982.5 / 1261.9 m/z, 0.9-2.8 % in 5C): transmitted like the parent ion (T relative to parent 0.59 (0.30-0.94) for 1103.9 in the 8+ channel, face-value 0.60 and 1.17 for 982.5 and 1261.9). Sanity check that the method does not invent selectivity at fixed z.
* The ~403 m/z ion (1.31 % in 5C, also 402.4 in 5B): T(403)/T(6+) = 3.05 face value (lower bound 2.4) in the 6+ channel, 1.59 (>=1.03) in the 7+ channel, 1.17 (>=0.50) in the 8+ channel, **< 0.15** in the 9+ channel (panel < 1.27 %). I.e. the low-mass ion is transmitted ~3x better than the channel's own ion at the 6+ resonance and not at all at 9+; this is a statement about relative transmission only. m/z 171 (4.4 % in A4, 1.25 % in 5C) and 1413 (5.0 %; 5C has the same shoulder at -12 m/z, 0.9 %) are transmitted ~0.56 and ~1.0 relative to 6+.
* Species seen in an A panel but not in 5C (330 in A3 and A4, 501, 575 in A4): lower bounds only (T >= 1.76, 0.37, 0.53 relative to 6+ in A4).

## 6. Peaks in 5A that are not the channel's own charge state (`fig5A_nonmain_peaks.csv`)

| panel (channel) | m/z (main-anchored) | m/z best estimate | height (%) | ubiquitin z? | in 5C? (height in 5C, % of 8+) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A1 (9+) | 857.5 | 857.5 | 8.55 | 10 | yes, 4.71 % at 857.2 |
| A1 (9+) | 982.5 | 982.5 | 3.6 | - | yes, 0.89 % at 981.4 |

| A2 (8+) | 403.3 | 402.6 | 1.54 | - | yes, 1.31 % at 402.6 |
| A2 (8+) | 952.8 | 952.8 | 1.54 | 9 | yes, 15.17 % at 952.5 |
| A2 (8+) | 1223.0 | 1223.0 | 1.54 | 7 | yes, 60.53 % at 1224.6 |
| A3 (7+) | 326.7 | 328.5 | 2.54 | - | no (<0.62) |
| A3 (7+) | 400.7 | 402.6 | 3.47 | - | yes, 1.31 % at 402.6 |
| A4 (6+) | 171.2 | 170.2 | 4.42 | - | yes, 1.25 % at 170.1 |
| A4 (6+) | 329.7 | 328.8 | 10.91 | - | no (<0.62) |
| A4 (6+) | 403.3 | 402.4 | 25.47 | - | yes, 1.31 % at 402.6 |
| A4 (6+) | 501.7 | 500.8 | 2.88 | - | no (<0.62) |
| A4 (6+) | 575.5 | 574.6 | 3.77 | - | no (<0.62) |
| A4 (6+) | 1412.8 | 1412.8 | 5.03 | - | yes, 0.89 % at 1416.6 |

* m/z precision: 1 sigma ~0.5-0.8 m/z for the best estimates (A4 330, 501, 575 are corrected by the +0.91 m/z offset that A4 shows on its two peaks shared with 5C, 171 and 403; A3 by -1.84 on its one shared peak; A3's 326.7 -> 328.5 then agrees with A4's 328.8). Values for peaks shared with 5B/5C: **402.6 +- 0.3, 170.1 +- 0.4 m/z** (5C calibrated on 5 printed labels).
* Charge/isotope spacing: **not resolvable** (3.07 m/z per pixel; a peak is 1-2 columns). Peaks at 171, 329, 403, 501, 575 are consistent with singly charged chemical background (no comment possible on z). 857.5 is the 10+ ion of ubiquitin (theory 857.49).
* Low-mass peaks are visible in the **same relative abundance order in v2 and v3** (A4: 330 10.4 vs 10.9 %, 403 24.8 vs 25.5 %). They are physical contents of the 6+ channel output, not plot artefacts. The 403 ion exists in the control (1.31 %, 2x floor) and in 5B (0.64 %), so it is not created by the channel; it is enriched ~3x relative to 6+ (section 5). 330 is absent from 5C and 5B (limits 0.62 / 0.52 %) but seen in A3 and A4 (2.5 and 10.9 %): its enrichment at the 6+/7+ channels is >= 1.8x (A4).
* In A1 the 982.5 (3.6 %) and 1003.5 (2.0 %) peaks are the +269/+457 Da sidebands of 9+ (5C: 0.89 / 0.84 %), not cross-talk. The shoulder at -12..-16 m/z (A4 1412.8, 5C 1416.6, B 1058.1 on 8+ at 12.7 %, B 1210.6 on 7+ at 3.0 %) is a satellite of the main ions (about -90..-110 Da) present in the control; **B has a 1058 shoulder (12.7 % of 8+) that no single-channel panel nor the control shows**, which is odd and worth asking about.
* No sign of a higher-order pass band at high m/z: z=5 (1714) and z=6/7 on the high-m/z side of the 9+/8+/7+ channels show nothing above the display limit in any panel (limits in the matrix).

## 7. Fig S14 (`figS14_*.csv`)

Panels: two Xcalibur screenshots (Part I = gate open, RT 0.98 min, scan 429, NL 1.82E6; Part II = AC on 83 kHz / 3 V, RT 1.18 min, scan 519, NL 4.64E5), each with the full TIC (same file, 0-3.06 min, NL 3.20E8) and one spectrum, 150-2000 m/z. There are no resonance-scan panels or AC on/off sweeps in S14; the only quantitative content is the two spectra and the TIC.

* x calibration: 100-m/z major ticks (13-14 identified per spectrum, rms 0.3 m/z); printed labels reproduce to <= 0.35 m/z (575.984 +0.04, 587.524 0.00, 654.331 -0.20, 728.403 -0.18, 874.466 -0.16, 978.532 +0.09, 863.473 0.00; 863.472 -0.33; the blended 530.788 +0.66). 1 px = 1.39 m/z, 0.27 % tall.
* **Na adduct (874.46 = 863.47 + 10.994):** Part I (gate open) 2.23 +- 0.56 % vs 24.98 +- 0.27 % -> adduct/main **0.089 +- 0.022**; Part II (AC on) 5.69 +- 0.84 % vs 99.56 +- 0.28 % -> **0.057 +- 0.009**. Ratio of ratios (adduct transmission relative to the main ion through the 83-kHz channel) = **0.64 +- 0.19** (printed-label estimate 0.62; consistent, now with an error bar). Baseline: Part I is grassy (p95 0.49 %, max 0.69 %), Part II p95 0.79 % (includes real small peaks).
  * Caveats: the two ions are 8 px apart, the adduct envelope is only 1-2 columns, and Part II labels the adduct 873.964 while Part I labels 874.466 (different isotope at the apex; the drawn pixel max is what is compared). Area ratios are not used.
* Main-ion counts, AC on / open: (99.56 % x 4.64e5) / (24.98 % x 1.82e6) = **1.016 +- 0.012** (previous 1.01 +- 0.05). The statement 90-100 % in the caption is a base-peak statement; the TIC cannot test it (below).
* Other ions in Part II (AC on): 854.74 (2.1 %; printed 853.967: our apex 0.8 m/z higher than the label, ~0.6 px), 882.42 (2.3 %; = main + 18.95 m/z = [M+K+H]2+, K adduct), 530.65 (1.35 %), 728.46 (1.24 %). Part I peak catalogue in `figS14_peak_catalog.csv` (30 peaks >= 1.5 %).
* TIC (`figS14_tic_levels.csv`; medians in windows because label text contaminates a point-by-point trace): open plateaus 8.9 % (cycles 1-2) and 11.6 % (cycles 3-4) of 3.2e8 (2.9e7 and 3.7e7 in NL units); closed (AC on) < ~0.3 % (< 1e6); the AC-on spectrum base peak is 0.145 % of NL, so the AC-on TIC is essentially the single 863.47 ion within the 0.25 %/px resolution. Part I and II TIC panels agree to 0.2 %.

## 8. Caveats

1. 5C is a separate control acquisition (direct transfer, no resonant excitation), not the measured input to each channel; ion abundance, space-charge and AGC differ between acquisitions. T ratios use it as the source.
2. Detector response per charge state (Orbitrap image current, m/z-dependent transfer) cancels in the double ratio only if it is the same in panel and control.
3. Panels are individually normalised; only within-panel ratios are meaningful, and 1 px = 0.74 % limits 5A heights near the floor to a factor ~2.
4. Peak height rather than area is used: each isotope line is sub-pixel at this resolution.
5. The x-axis tick marks in Fig 5 do not match the data (offsets -4..+10 m/z): do not calibrate Fig 5 from ticks.
6. Whether the plotting software suppresses low peaks: v1/v2 show baseline blips down to 0.7 %, v3/published shows none below ~1.2 % -> suppression/thresholding in the final redraw is likely; the true spectra were noisier at the ~1 % level and any claim below ~1.2-1.5 % is out of reach for 5A.
7. The four A panels do not share a base peak: nothing here gives the absolute transmission per channel or the resolution R (the neighbour-to-channel ratio gives a lower-bound flavour of R only through Lorentzian assumptions that I did not make).
8. Uncertainties (+-1 px on all heights) are bounds from quantisation, not statistical confidence intervals.

fig2C_I_over_I0_vs_N.csv.text:
# Fig 2C: normalised intensity I/I0 of singly charged ions vs number of available (low-barrier) output ports N, 1134Q (per text; panel itself only says 'N'), ions 1+..6+, from five-peptide mixture. Raster digitization of the v3 bioRxiv figure bitmap (1100x1841 px; same data as v2 and the published f2 image).
# Axis calibration: x from tick-label centres 0..1200 (143.0 px = 0, 0.7360 px per N); y from label centres 0..1 (0 at 1737.5 px; 477.5 px per unit). # Fig S14: 2+ ion m/z 863.47 (Bak BH3 peptide) and its Na adduct ([M+Na+H]2+, +10.994 m/z, printed 874.466 / 873.964). Part I = gate OPEN (RT 0.98 min, scan 429, NL 1.82E6); Part II = AC ON 83 kHz 3 V (RT 1.18 min, scan 519, NL 4.64E5).
# SOURCE SM PDF p.21/p.22 native rasters (1396x1074, 1422x1038), BITMAP. Heights = apex pixel column of each envelope within +-2.5 m/z of the expected position (1 px = 1.39 m/z merges the 0.5-m/z isotope lines, so the drawn height is the envelope apex, same for both ions). Areas are NOT used: each isotope line is sub-pixel wide, so a pixel sum measures the line rendering, not the signal.
# Uncertainty on a height = sqrt((1 px = 0.27 %)^2 + (p95 of the empty baseline within +-40 m/z)^2); ratios by quadrature. Part I baseline p95 0.49 %, Part II 0.79 % (this includes real small peaks at 854.7 and 882).
